name: MHRA: domperidone and phaeochromocytoma
summary: The MHRA says domperidone is now contraindicated in confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma because of a risk of severe hypertension.
keyPoints: The MHRA published a Drug Safety Update on 21 July 2026 about domperidone.
Domperidone is now contraindicated in patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma.
The reason is a risk of severe hypertension (very high blood pressure).
The MHRA had received no UK Yellow Card reports of this event.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says a recent European review of safety data identified an association between domperidone and episodes of severe hypertension in patients with phaeochromocytoma, after a small number of reports. Phaeochromocytoma is a rare tumour of the adrenal gland.

As a result, domperidone is now contraindicated in patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma, which means it should not be used in them.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA tells prescribers that patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma who are taking domperidone should have treatment stopped and be switched to an alternative. It adds that domperidone can unmask the tumour, so a severe hypertensive episode in someone taking it should prompt consideration of further investigation.

The MHRA says it has not received any UK Yellow Card reports of severe hypertension with domperidone in patients with phaeochromocytoma, and asks that suspected side effects be reported through the Yellow Card scheme. Anyone with questions about their own treatment can ask the prescriber or pharmacist.

source.title: Domperidone: new contraindication in patients with phaeochromocytoma due to the risk of severe hypertension
